Hi Ben,

Quick intro — I lead ML infra at Finnova. We're evaluating vendors for an embeddings pipeline and I wanted a baseline from Redwood before we kick off a formal RFP. Two quick questions to start:

1) How do you bill embeddings — per-vector, per-token, or a hybrid? We have short pieces of text that map to 1536-dim vectors.
2) Which embedding model variants/dimensions do you support today (1536 / 1024 / 768)? Any model names we should reference?

Context: anticipated pilot is ~10M vectors/month, long-term could grow to 50–100M. Any volume-discount ranges or committed pricing tiers are helpful. Also curious about batching limits and typical latency for a 1536-vector single-call.

If you prefer, send a short rate card and I'll share with procurement.

Thanks —
Alice

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings pricing + dims & model support

Hi Alice — thanks for reaching out and the clear context. Happy to help.

Short answers up front:
- We bill embeddings per-vector (rounded to the nearest request) for calls that directly generate vectors.
- We support 1536- and 1024-dim variants across our Redwood-verified models and a set of vetted open models; 768-dim legacy models available by request.

I'm attaching our current embeddings rate card (PDF) which lists baseline per-vector rates and tiered discounts. For your pilot (10M/month) expect a ~10% committed discount vs on-demand; larger committed volumes get higher discounts — details in the attached.

A few notes you might find useful:
- If you run a text->embedding pipeline where you also use the hosted text tokenizer, there can be minor token usage charges for the tokenizer/preprocessing step; embedding vectors themselves are per-vector.
- We recommend batching up to 512 vectors per request for throughput; single-request latency for a 1536-dim vector (small batch) is typically 30–70ms p95 in hosted regions, dependent on concurrency.

I've looped in Marissa (pricing) and Dev (product) to confirm exact tier math and whether a custom model mapping is needed for Finnova's use-case.

Attachment: redwood-embeddings-ratecard-v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Best,
Ben Carter

Ben — answering inline and adding the bits you can pass to Alice.

1) Baseline pricing (on-demand / per-vector):
- embed-redwood-1536: $0.00042 per vector (on-demand)
- embed-open-1024: $0.00030 per vector (on-demand)
- embed-legacy-768: $0.00020 per vector (available on request)

Notes: All embeddings are billed per-vector for the returned vector payload. If customers also use hosted tokenizer endpoints as a separate call, tokenized input may incur small token charges — we should call that out but it's typically negligible for short inputs.

2) Committed discounts (12-month term suggestions):
- 10M vectors/month -> 10% off on-demand (effective price for embed-redwood-1536 would be $0.000378/vector)
- 50M vectors/month -> 18% off on-demand
- 100M+ -> custom pricing / sales + finance approval (usually 25%+ depending on commitment and SLA)

3) Supported model identifiers / dims (recommended copy for the customer):
- embed-redwood-1536 (1536 dims, high-quality semantic vectors, lowest latency)
- embed-open-1024 (1024 dims, good tradeoff of quality/cost)
- embed-legacy-768 (768 dims, smaller index footprint)

4) Performance guidance / batching:
- Recommended batch sizing: 128–512 vectors per request for best throughput.
- Typical single-call p95 latency (1536 dim): 30–70ms depending on region & concurrency.
- Max soft limit per request: 2048 vectors; we suggest streaming/batching for very large bulk loads.

5) Attachments / links to pass to the customer:
- redwood-embeddings-ratecard-v1.pdf (attached)
- https://docs.redwood.ai/embeddings/pricing (public pricing details & billing semantics)

6) Discount negotiation guidance:
- For procurement, offer the 10% pilot discount with a 60-day pilot clause and an option to convert to a 12-month committed tier if they hit 10M for two consecutive months. That reduces friction and protects both sides.

Let me know if you want me to co-sign an email to procurement or if you want a short pricing one-pager tailored to 10M/50M bands.

—Marissa
